questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That they spoke spanish down here, because I really wanted to improve my spanish. The weather was also a factor, and that you have the beach very close. I love also doing a lot of sports, playing football, padel tennis, tennis and so forth and I knew that these sports are being played a lot in Spain and thereby of course Barcelona as well.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly medium I would say. When you first found the course catalogue it was okay, and then also I would add that the incoming coordinator was very good at answering your questions both over phone and email, she speaks englise quite well also.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: When I arrived it was very easy. You just go the university's international office and they sort you out with everything and also a week later, there is a big day for all the exchange students where you get to meet each other and ask questions there as well and so forth.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was fairly difficult, we spent a lot of time on it me and two friends. We ended up going the 'Housinganywhere' which had some expensive fees, but I would recommend maybe finding some shared housing if you go alone, through some facebook groups or similar. Or if booking with friends, look at Airbnb in good time.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would say that living in El Raval is not as dangerous as people say, I didn't but have loads of friends who did. I would have loved to live in San Antoni or Gracia.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's somewhat expensive, but it's also what'd you expect from a metropolitan city as Barcelona.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was very easy. There was an online portal where you just chose your desired destinations and found some courses that the university offered and yeah, quite easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much really. There was a seminar regarding this, but you didn't really need that much help I would say.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 100% successful, so that was nice.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would say that you find the schedules and the exam dates ahead of time, so maybe in an ideal world I would have organized my subjects so that I could travel home a week before.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses is relatively lower compared to the University of Copenhagen. It is easier to pass the courses also because there is continuous evalutation and the required level of math is very low. What challenged was that for two courses I had to make research proposals based on exisisting scholarly articles, which is something I hadn't done before.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It's very different. The classes are way smaller and there is large focus on scholarly articles and writing reports about this. Also we had to make a lot of presentations which is something I never did at my home university, and as i said, the research proposals.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Economic Growth, Game Theory, Macroeconometrics, Microeconometrics, Empirical Approach to Economic Growth, Welfare Economics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I quite liked game theory, also because it was the only course with proper math and it challenged. Also the welfare economics is very different from back home and gave different perspectives to what I am used to.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I though I could use the EU data through my danish supplier, but i couldn't after three months. A speeding ticket from a rental car :))

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The public is really good and very cheap, it's 20 euros a month for all the public transport, it even takes you to the airport and to the small beaches outside the city.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is both padel tennis and tennis offered through UB sports, it was 40 euros for 12 group classes and it was really fun social and cheap.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the app 'Celebreak' if you're into football. You can play all over Barcelona with other people and it's a really nice way to meet new folks and just play. Also hiking trips in northern catalunya, such as Mont Rebei and a trip to Costa Brava to cliff jump and chill out.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Just chill up in Gracia and if you go to the beach, for god's sake dont go to Barceloneta but go to Platja de Bogatell.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy for me. I love the laid-back culture of no stress, eating late and stuff like this so.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Yea, as I said, the 'Celebreak' app and the tennis classes. Otherwise just keep an open mind, there are a lot internationals down here, and everyone wants to make friends, so just don't be scared of starting a conversation.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The "manana-manana" vibe, and the vibe that you meet late and there is no pressure on getting absolutely hammered when you go out as in Denmark, you can just chill have a few beers and then also be ready for the next day and I enjoyed that.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: The academic level is lower. The class 'Economic Growth' can be taken as a seminar. Can't think of a third.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The new people, the time for sports and exercise, the hiking trips, the laid-backness, the opportunity to not stress around with job and school and have so much more free-time, so that you can say yes to anything.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Probably missing my girl.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
